::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Resources: Quarto websites

-   [Creating a Website](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/) (the Quarto guide this chapter follows)
-   [Video: Build a Quarto website in RStudio](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l7r24gTEkEY) (the video embedded below)
-   [Publish Your Report to Quarto Pub](quartopub.qmd) (the same `quarto publish` steps work for a website)
:::

An academic website is a place to put your name, your research interests, your CV, and links to your reports and posters, so that a professor, a graduate program, or an employer can find your work in one place. You already have the skills to build one. A Quarto website is a folder of `.qmd` files, exactly like the reports you wrote in this playbook, plus one `_quarto.yml` file that lists the pages and gives the site its navigation bar. You write in markdown ([Write an Introduction](write-intro.qmd)), you click Render, and you publish with the same `quarto publish quarto-pub` command you used in [Publish Your Report to Quarto Pub](quartopub.qmd). Your published reports can then be linked from, or copied into, the site.

The two resources below are the whole chapter. The Quarto guide explains what a website project is, what goes in `_quarto.yml`, and how to add pages, a navigation bar, and an About page. The video shows one being built in RStudio from File \> New Project onward, so watch it with RStudio open and build your site alongside it.

::: callout-tip
## Go: read the guide, then build along with the video

1.  Open [Creating a Website](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/) and read the page from the top through the *RStudio* tab under *Quick Start*. That tab is the one for you: it creates the website project the same way you created `Lastname_FRI`.
2.  Watch the video below with RStudio open, and build your own site as it goes. Keep the site in its own project folder, not inside `Lastname_FRI`.
3.  When your site renders, publish it the way you published your report: run `quarto publish quarto-pub` in the RStudio Terminal from the site's folder.
